plans.executive_summary: Incident INC-01 details a critical compromise of the SSH server (ssh-srv) originating from external IP 203.0.113.13. The attack sequence started with port scanning (T1595.001), followed by credential brute-force (T1110) which successfully compromised the 'deploy' user account, escalated privileges via sudo to root, and culminated in unauthorized large-scale data exfiltration over port 4444 to external IP 198.51.100.200 (T1041).

immediate_actions.action: Block attacker IP address at the firewall
Block exfiltration destination IP address at the firewall
Isolate the compromised SSH server from the internal network for forensics
immediate_actions.example_command: ip link set dev eth0 down

immediate_actions.action: Disable compromised user account and force credential resets

investigation_steps: Review authentication logs on ssh-srv around 2026-10-16T20:55:18Z to analyze the exact mechanism and scope of the credential brute-force and subsequent privilege escalation.
Examine network flow logs and full packet captures (PCAP) to determine the exact volume and nature of data transferred to 198.51.100.200 over port 4444.
Perform a comprehensive forensic disk and memory analysis on ssh-srv (10.0.0.10) to identify any backdoors, modified binaries, or unauthorized persistence mechanisms.
Audit sudoers configuration and authorization logs to verify all actions taken by the 'deploy' user after successful privilege escalation.
prevention: Implement Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) for all SSH access, eliminating reliance solely on passwords.
Enforce strict account lockout policies and rate-limiting for SSH login attempts to mitigate brute-force and password spraying attacks.
Deploy network intrusion detection and prevention systems (IDS/IPS) to monitor and block abnormal outbound data transfers over non-standard ports like port 4444.
Regularly audit user and service account privileges, ensuring the Principle of Least Privilege is strictly maintained for sudo access.
